description: Routing metadata from declared abstract issue signals to existing C27 discovery checks and source owners. This is not a legal-rule registry, fact extractor, or proof of execution.
input_boundary: The selector CLI accepts only synthetic_abstract fixtures containing opaque proceeding IDs and declared signal IDs. Its select_check_ids API accepts only registered signal IDs and is used by the privacy-minimised route receipt gate. Neither path accepts narratives, jurisdictions, dates, identities, documents, or other free-text fields.

eu_common_core.owner: EU and common free-movement law, CJEU interpretation, and EU guidance; maintained by the core
eu_common_core.currentness_rule: Resolve the matching registered EU pack and check official current text before relying on a source for a current consultation. A pinned compatibility copy or handbook does not establish currentness or binding status.

member_state_law.owner: National law, competent institutions, procedural remedies, and national deadlines belong to the module for the deciding or challenged Member State
member_state_law.currentness_rule: Use only an available, matching module and verified official national sources. If absent or incomplete, keep the national issue open and qualify only conclusions that depend on it.

applicant_country_operations.owner: Mission channels, appointment practice, local document acquisition, and operational facts belong to the applicant-country module
applicant_country_operations.currentness_rule: Check current official mission or provider information. Do not use local operational practice to redefine EU legal rights.

eu_swiss_framework.owner: EU–Swiss free-movement arrangements are a distinct treaty framework; do not apply Directive 2004/38/EC to a Swiss refusal by default
eu_swiss_framework.official_source_query: Retrieve and verify the applicable Agreement on the Free Movement of Persons and relevant official EU and Swiss material at EUR-Lex or Fedlex.
eu_swiss_framework.currentness_rule: The bundled Swiss source-library records are candidate discovery material; the Swiss library states that zero sources are accepted. Verify official text and applicability independently before drawing a legal conclusion.

eu_data_protection.owner: EU data-protection law belongs to EU/common core; national supervisory competence and procedure belong to the relevant Member-State module
eu_data_protection.official_source_query: Check the official GDPR text and the competent supervisory authority's current procedure where the issue is factually triggered.
eu_data_protection.currentness_rule: Do not infer a data-protection grievance from an ordinary procedural dispute. Distinguish preservation, access, retention, and supervisory complaints.

signal_catalog.neutral_description: Personal, material, or territorial scope of a claimed Directive-based family route is in issue.
The family member's travel or residence link to the moving Union citizen is in issue.
A prior refusal or a change in relationship, movement, or legal status may affect the present question.
A Swiss or EU–Swiss free-movement route may govern a refusal or family-rights question.
An appointment, access, or attempted-lodgement event may have prevented an application from being received.
A visa application centre or other external service provider participates in the process.
A fee charged by or through an external provider is disputed.
The abstract scenario expressly has no disputed external-provider fee.
A document demand or ordinary checklist may be affecting an EU-family application.
A specific document demand is part of the abstract issue.
A requested document is unavailable or its evidentiary effect is disputed.
A processing period, pre-lodgement delay, clock trigger, or deadline is in issue.
The abstract scenario declares that formal lodging is confirmed.
A formal challenge deadline may be running or at risk.
A formal appeal, SOLVIT matter, or supervisory/process complaint is in issue.
The abstract scenario declares a formal refusal decision.
A SOLVIT process is pending or proposed.
A specific processing, access, purpose, retention, or supervisory issue involving personal data is in scope.
Potentially relevant time-limited evidence, such as an incident recording, may be lost.
The specific record being preserved contains identifiable personal data.
The Union citizen may be returning to their own Member State after qualifying movement.
Qualifying movement or a cross-border topology is alleged or queried.
The claimed family relationship or its recognition is in issue.
The abstract timeline places a prior refusal before a claimed relationship or legal-status change.
Appointment access or waiting time is specifically in issue.
Reported physical exclusion or staff treatment may require separate review.
A distinct staff-conduct concern is in issue.

routes.neutral_description: Assess whether the claimed family route falls within the personal, material, and territorial scope of the Directive.
triggering_conditions: A Directive-based entitlement, visa facilitation, or residence right is actually raised as an issue.

conditional_checks.reason: Movement or cross-border topology is expressly in issue.
A returning Union citizen may require separate EU and national returnee analysis.
Recognition or proof of the relationship is expressly disputed.

review_topics: competing legal regime
territorial or personal-scope exception
contrary authority or fact that changes the claimed topology

negative_applicability: A generic visa enquiry, provider fee, or complaint alone does not activate this route.

routes.neutral_description: Assess whether the family member accompanies or joins the Union citizen in the relevant movement or residence situation.
triggering_conditions: The travel, arrival, or residence relationship between the family member and Union citizen is relevant to the requested legal outcome.

conditional_checks.reason: A returnee route requires its own scope analysis.
Relationship status or recognition is expressly in issue.

review_topics: different travel dates or travel sequence
whether movement is qualifying
family status and any recognised exception

negative_applicability: A family member's travel question without a claimed Union-citizen movement link does not by itself establish Directive coverage.

routes.neutral_description: Keep historical refusal events separate and assess whether a later relationship or status change affects the present proceeding.
triggering_conditions: A prior refusal, later change in legal status, or claimed carry-over effect is material to the current question.

conditional_checks.reason: The abstract chronology places an earlier refusal before a claimed status change; assess each proceeding and any later decision separately.
A declared formal refusal may engage a separate appeal and service clock.

review_topics: which legal status existed at each event
whether the prior decision is being treated as a current ground without support
whether service or a later decision creates a separate deadline

negative_applicability: An application, appointment, or complaint alone does not establish a prior refusal or a later status change.

routes.neutral_description: Identify whether the EU–Swiss free-movement framework, rather than the Directive, governs the Swiss-related issue.
triggering_conditions: A Swiss national, Swiss authority, or EU–Swiss agreement is material to the legal route.

conditional_checks.reason: Relationship status or proof is separately in issue.
A formal Swiss decision requires its own actual grounds and remedy route.

source_references: Official EU–Swiss Agreement on the Free Movement of Persons text at EUR-Lex or Fedlex

review_topics: Directive versus bilateral-agreement legal basis
personal and material scope of the agreement
Swiss domestic implementation and available remedy

negative_applicability: Do not select this route solely because a Swiss location or a generic European free-movement question is mentioned.

routes.neutral_description: Separate appointment and access obstruction from formal refusal after examination.
triggering_conditions: An appointment request, physical attendance, or submission attempt may have been delayed, blocked, or refused before formal lodging.

conditional_checks.reason: The access delay is specifically declared and may affect practical effectiveness or evidence preservation.
Reported staff treatment or physical exclusion must be considered as a distinct conduct track.

review_topics: appointment access versus a decision on the merits
evidence of attempted submission and any receipt
the exact legal basis for direct access or use of a service provider

negative_applicability: Do not label a pre-lodgement access event a formal visa refusal without a formal decision.

routes.neutral_description: Assess a provider's procedural role and keep provider fees distinct from the visa fee.
triggering_conditions: An external visa service provider participates in the application route.

conditional_checks.reason: A disputed provider fee requires separation from the visa fee and assessment under the relevant EU-family regime.

negative_applicability.reason: When no provider-fee dispute is declared, do not select fee-specific checks merely because a provider is used.

review_topics: visa fee versus optional provider service fee
the Member State's responsibility for outsourced processing
direct access rule, if any, under the exact applicable arrangement

routes.neutral_description: Compare an ordinary document list with the requirements and limits for an EU-family application.
triggering_conditions: A document demand, checklist, or proof issue may affect an EU-family visa or free-movement entitlement.

conditional_checks.reason: A specific demand may require comparison with the applicable national and provider instructions.
A missing item may affect proof without automatically preventing an independent legal conclusion.

review_topics: ordinary checklist applicability to the applicant category
the item's actual purpose and legal basis
alternative proof, proportionality, and any specific exception

negative_applicability: Do not activate this route for an unrelated ordinary visitor checklist unless an EU-family or free-movement issue is also declared.

routes.neutral_description: Identify the applicable processing rule and the event that starts its clock; keep appointment delay separate.
triggering_conditions: The user asks about delay, processing time, a deadline, or the effect of an uncertain lodging date.

conditional_checks.reason: Formal lodging is declared; verify the clock's event, any allowed extension, and any suspension.
An appeal deadline may be distinct from the visa-processing clock and must be protected.

review_topics: enquiry, appointment, and formal lodging as different clock events
legal basis and any exception or extension
parallel appeal deadline that a complaint does not suspend

negative_applicability: A complaint or appointment question alone does not activate this route unless a processing delay, clock, or deadline issue is declared.

routes.neutral_description: Identify formal appeal, informal problem-solving, and supervisory or conduct routes without merging them.
triggering_conditions: A formal challenge, SOLVIT process, or supervisory/process complaint is requested or already pending.

conditional_checks.reason: A formal refusal or at-risk deadline requires separate verification of the national appeal route and clock.
SOLVIT is a distinct process and does not replace or suspend a formal appeal deadline.
A service or conduct grievance has an independent subject and outcome.

review_topics: formal decision versus administrative grievance
competent body and exact power to grant the requested relief
parallel routes and preserved deadlines

negative_applicability: A complaint label alone does not create a statutory visa appeal or prove that a formal decision exists.

routes.neutral_description: Review GDPR scope and data-processing issues only when a concrete personal-data issue is declared.
triggering_conditions: The issue specifically concerns the purpose, necessity, access, retention, or supervision of personal-data processing.

conditional_checks.reason: A personal-data record is declared at risk; assess prompt preservation separately from access.

source_references: Official GDPR text and current competent supervisory-authority procedure

review_topics: whether the issue is actually about personal data
purpose, necessity, and the precise controller
national supervisory competence and any scope exception

negative_applicability: Do not select GDPR checks solely because a visa application, complaint, or non-personal evidence-preservation request exists.

routes.neutral_description: Preserve concrete time-limited evidence promptly; add data-protection checks only when the record contains personal data.
triggering_conditions: A specific record may be deleted, overwritten, or otherwise become unavailable before a later complaint or review.

conditional_checks.reason: The record is declared to contain personal data; check GDPR-specific preservation and controller issues.
The threatened record may support a separate conduct issue.

review_topics: specific record and likely deletion or overwrite time
competent holder and proportionate preservation request
whether the record contains personal data, which would add a separate GDPR question

negative_applicability: Do not select an urgent preservation route from a generic complaint or records request without evidence at risk of loss.
